task: Preserve the exact nested parent proof/persistence exception at the release executor machine-error boundary so a blocked parent closure reports both the stable blocker code and its exact root cause without changing fail-closed semantics.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Release Unit Execution #260 (`37731330506`) successfully closed U03 through the governed ALREADY_APPLIED no-code path and advanced the parent to closureEligible=true / TRUTH_GATE, but parent closure then failed outwardly only as RELEASE_PARENT_PROOF_OR_PERSISTENCE_FAILED. `closeParentReleaseExecution()` already preserves the exact inner exception in `result.error`; `scripts/release-unit-execute.mjs` discards it whenever `result.reason` exists by serializing `result.reason ?? result.error`. This reproduces open Failure Intake #1018 (TRUSTED_EXECUTOR_EXCEPTION_LOG_ONLY) and violates the hardening requirement that authoritative gates/executors expose exact machine-readable root cause without a second log/API hunt.
observableOutcomes: A BLOCK result from the release executor emits a machine-readable payload containing the stable `reason` and the exact nested `error` simultaneously when both exist.
Existing blocker code semantics remain unchanged; diagnostic enrichment cannot convert BLOCK into PENDING/PASS or alter release-state transitions.
Parent proof/persistence failures continue to fail closed but expose the exact child command/guard exception directly in the workflow error.

Regression coverage on the non-receipt-bound execution-binding surface proves the driver uses a whitelisted `{reason,error}` payload, preserves null normalization for either missing field, and no longer uses reason/error nullish coalescing.
Post-merge immutable source replay resumes from canonical state with U03 already CLOSED and reveals the exact remaining parent closure root cause directly.
unresolvedRisks: Replacing the stable blocker reason with only a raw exception would make automation brittle and lose the normalized failure class.
Serializing arbitrary result objects could leak unrelated state or secrets; only reason and error may be surfaced.
Changing parent closure proof behavior in the same transaction would conflate observability hardening with the still-unknown root-cause repair.
Editing persisted rehearsal state manually would invalidate resumability proof.

in: Add a minimal pure diagnostic payload formatter at the release executor boundary.
Serialize both normalized reason and exact nested error for BLOCK decisions.
Add regression tests for reason+error, reason-only and error-only payload shapes.
Preserve the existing parent helper, closure proof, Truth, persistence and CAS semantics.
out: No change to release-unit state-machine transitions.
No change to scripts/release-unit-parent-close.mjs proof or persistence behavior.
No change to immutable source branch/SHA.
No threshold, Truth, Sentinel, risk, lifecycle or receipt relaxation.
No storefront, template, Supabase or deployment change.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is an observability-only change on a write-capable release executor. It must expose exact failure detail while preserving the stable blocker class, fail-closed behavior, state CAS semantics and least-privilege execution surface.

acceptanceCriteria: BLOCK with `{reason:'R',error:'E'}` produces a machine error that contains both `reason:'R'` and `error:'E'`.
BLOCK with reason only preserves the normalized reason and emits null/absent exact error deterministically.
BLOCK with error only preserves the exact error and emits null/absent normalized reason deterministically.
The executor still throws and exits non-zero for every BLOCK.
No release-state, parent proof, persistence, Truth or lifecycle semantics change.
Exact-head CI and lifecycle closure pass before merge.
Post-merge replay of immutable source `65e52ffd...` exposes the exact parent closure root cause without separate log hunting.
invariants: Stable blocker reason remains available to machine consumers.
Exact nested error is additive diagnostic evidence, not authority.
No secrets or whole result/state object are serialized.
Persisted release-state remains executor-owned and CAS-protected.
U03 remains CLOSED and is not reopened or duplicated.

diagnostic formatter serializes entire result and leaks unrelated fields

parent state already closureEligible with activeUnitId null

specialistReviews.finding: A tempting implementation is to alter parent-close error handling or parent proof commands at the same time as diagnostic surfacing, but the exact failing command is not yet observable.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep parent-close runtime read-only in this transaction; patch only the outer serialization boundary, then use the next replay to reveal the exact root cause.

specialistReviews.finding: Diagnostic expansion must avoid dumping state or environment.
specialistReviews.resolution: Whitelist only normalized reason and exact error fields.

specialistReviews.finding: U03 is CLOSED with ALREADY_APPLIED no-code proof; the active blocker is parent closure diagnostics/root cause.
specialistReviews.resolution: Do not touch U03 or persisted state; replay after merge resumes at parent closure.

specialistReviews.finding: Open Failure Intake #1018 already defines this exact observability failure class.
specialistReviews.resolution: Attach #260 reproduction to #1018 and add deterministic regression proof.

challenge.scenario: Release Unit Execution #260 returns `{reason:'RELEASE_PARENT_PROOF_OR_PERSISTENCE_FAILED', error:'<exact child command failure>'}` from `closeParentReleaseExecution()`, while the outer driver still evaluates `result.reason ?? result.error`.
challenge.finding: The emitted workflow exception contains only `RELEASE_PARENT_PROOF_OR_PERSISTENCE_FAILED`; the exact nested parent proof/persistence exception is deterministically discarded and requires a second investigation path.
challenge.resolution: Replace the coalescing boundary with a whitelisted diagnostic payload that serializes both fields as `{reason,error}` while retaining the same BLOCK throw and non-zero exit.

challenge.scenario: Throw only the raw nested error.

A BLOCK result also contains execution state, receipts, branch identity, or environment-derived data in addition to `reason` and `error`, and the outer driver serializes the entire result for convenience.
challenge.finding: The write-capable executor would expose unrelated authoritative state and potentially sensitive diagnostics merely to preserve one nested exception.
challenge.resolution: Whitelist exactly two outward fields—`reason` and `error`—and add regression coverage that no other result property is present in the serialized blocker payload.

challenge.scenario: Patch parent state so closure can retry differently.
challenge.finding: Would destroy resumability proof and hide the defect.
challenge.resolution: No state edits; canonical replay only.

challenge.scenario: Guess which parent proof command failed and patch it now.
challenge.finding: Current outer surface masks the exact exception; any such patch would be speculative.
challenge.resolution: Expose the exact error first, then make a second bounded root-cause repair only if needed.

challenge.scenario: A BLOCK result has `reason` but no nested `error`, as with a direct deterministic state-machine guard.
challenge.finding: A formatter that assumes `error` exists could throw while handling the original blocker and obscure the stable reason.
challenge.resolution: Normalize missing error to null while preserving the original reason and BLOCK exit.

challenge.scenario: A BLOCK result has an exact `error` but no normalized `reason`, for example a future adapter propagates an unclassified authoritative exception.
challenge.finding: A formatter that requires reason would recreate the current masking problem in the opposite direction.
challenge.resolution: Normalize missing reason to null while preserving the exact error verbatim.

challenge.scenario: The exact nested error contains quotes, newlines or stderr text from a failed child command.
challenge.finding: Manual string concatenation could produce ambiguous or unparsable machine output.
challenge.resolution: Continue using JSON serialization of the whitelisted `{reason,error}` payload so escaping is deterministic.

Merge only after exact PR-head SUCCESS and post-merge main CI SUCCESS.
Replay immutable source `65e52ffd1fd32f14353467eb7c52b2e06ba1be65`; because U03 is already CLOSED, require resume directly into parent closure and capture the exact nested error.
Fix the revealed parent root cause in the same hardening cycle if the replay still blocks.

requirements.requirement: Every fail-closed release executor BLOCK must retain its normalized reason and surface the exact nested authoritative error when present, without changing transition semantics or exposing unrelated state.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A normalized BLOCK reason may not mask an available exact nested executor error.
Diagnostic enrichment may not change BLOCK to PENDING/PASS or alter state persistence.
The diagnostic boundary may not serialize complete state/result/environment objects.

requirements.requirement: Parent closure remains bound to final implementation main and existing Completion Truth/Lifecycle authorities while observability is improved.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No diagnostic change may bypass or weaken parent Completion Truth, lifecycle, exact-main or persistence requirements.

notes: Live state after Release Unit Execution #260: U03 is CLOSED, materialization status ALREADY_APPLIED, verification VERIFIED/LEARN, noCode=true close receipt PASS; parent activeUnitId=null, closureEligible=true, closureComplete=false, lifecyclePhase=TRUTH_GATE. #260 then failed only as RELEASE_PARENT_PROOF_OR_PERSISTENCE_FAILED because the outer executor masks the exact `result.error` whenever `result.reason` exists. Open Failure Intake #1018 already covers this diagnostic class and has been updated with the #260 reproduction.
